content:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up -- hitting a nasty interaction between paged/blocked KV tombstones and the attention kernel's assumption of contiguous pinned KV addresses. Repro attached below.

cheng: Hmm. Can you paste the log snippet? Is this the case where compaction leaves small tombstone holes between live blocks?

maria: Yup. Example: allocator freed 8x4KB blocks scattered after eviction. The attention kernel does linear range scanning during KV lookup which assumes contiguous pages for the fast path. We see a ~12% tail token latency on long contexts.

noah: That linear scan is the culprit. Our optimized kernel uses a single memory region for KV cache to get pointer arithmetic in the hot loop. Fragmentation forces fallback to hashmap lookups and kills the vectorized path.

maria: Two straightforward options I see: 1) keep the kernel's contiguous assumption and force compaction/coalescing at eviction time (expensive), or 2) introduce a small cohabitation shim that presents a contiguous virtual view to the kernel but keeps physical paging. Thoughts? :thinking:

cheng: Option 2 sounds promising. We could add a 'kv_range_reserve' API the runtime calls before pinning. Kernel gets a logical contiguous range id, and the shim maintains a scatter-gather mapping. That keeps kernel ABI unchanged.

noah: Agree. Need to ensure the shim overhead is micro-optimized. The hot loop cannot deref an extra map per token. Proposal: expose a thin base pointer + stride table that the kernel can load into registers once per generate call.

maria: Prototype sketch (pseudo-config):
```
kv.cache.mode = "cohabitant"    # runtime provides sg-map to kernel
kv.coalesce_threshold = 0.2     # if fragmentation >20% consider forced coalesce
```

cheng: Implementation notes: reserve_range(range_len) returns (base_handle, sg_entries[]). Kernel receives base_handle and a single indirection table of up to 8 SG entries; anything >8 falls back to safe codepath. This keeps fast path for common cases.

noah: Good. We should also add an eviction hook so kernel can opt-in for async prefetch/rehydration of SG entries. Otherwise you'll get accidental page faults during generation.

maria: Right. Also need policy for tombstones: compact-on-idle vs background merge. Background merge might cause jitter in pinned range addresses unless we do epoched swaps. Suggest: epoch id in reserve_range; kernel only relies on mapping valid for given epoch; swap is atomic at epoch boundary.

cheng: Epoched swaps + CAS on mapping sounds safe. We'll need a small handshake:
```
int reserve_range(size_t len);
int publish_epoch(uint64_t epoch_id);
```
Kernel checks epoch before using mapping. If mismatch, fallback to safe path and retry.

infra-bot: deploy/cluster: perf-test-cluster updated with kernel-shim branch cheng/kv-shim @ 2099990020

maria: Perf numbers from the canary so far: with SG map <=4 entries we see <2% tail delta. With random fragmentation >30% and SG entries >8, we see fallback and ~15% tail. So goal: keep typical SG entries small and tune allocator to prefer coalescing when contiguous runs exist.

noah: Action items: I'll add microbench harness that simulates tombstone distributions and measures hot-loop overhead for 1/2/4/8 SG entries.

cheng: I'll push kernel shim prototype and the epoch API. Will also add the protected prefetch hook.

maria: I'll update rollout policy: canary on dedicated clusters, rule: if perc99 tokens > baseline +5% then automatic rollback. Also write a short runbook for debugging SG fallbacks.

noah: Add tests: synthetic fragmentation fixture + integration test that asserts no page faults during steady-state generation.

maria: OK scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00 PDT to review prototypes. @cheng @noah please bring perf graphs and a minimal patch set.

cheng: SG. I'll post the branch link in this thread before the meeting.

noah: Adding perf harness PR after lunch.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone hits weird OOMs while testing, tag me.

cheng: noted. :sparkles:
